items.title: Zhongshan International Youth Hostel
items.description: Concept “Holding Hands” — one person needs both hands to be strong, and a group is stronger still. The handshake shapes the façade; inside, guests can rest alone or share space with friends, with planted terraces on every level.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Lane 46, Zhongshan N. Rd. Sec. 2, Taipei

sections.heading: Concept — Holding Hands
sections.text: Two hands clasped together: one person needs both hands to be strong, and a group is stronger still. The handshake shapes the building's exterior. Inside, guests can rest on their own or share space with friends — a place that offers good service, a pleasant environment and the togetherness a group needs.

sections.heading: Site
sections.text: A 4–6 minute walk from Zhongshan and Shuanglian MRT stations, surrounded by shopping, hotels, salons and food streets with a young crowd.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: Curtain-wall glazing brings ventilation and daylight into the rooms, and planted terraces on every level give the building warmth. A rooftop café and terrace offer a shared place to meet.

items.title: Glory Building — NTUST Digital Construction Center
items.titleZh: 光榮大樓 台科大數位構築中心
items.description: Concept “The Graduation Cap” — a glazed cylindrical core forms the daylit crown of the building, while two wings hold studios, workshops, a library and research spaces around campus plazas.

sections.heading: Concept — The Graduation Cap
sections.text: The design is inspired by a graduation cap. The glazed cylindrical core — the crown of the cap — is the daylit heart of the building, while the two wings on either side hold teaching and research spaces.

sections.heading: Programme
sections.text: Lobby, administration, R&D studios, workshops, equipment and material storage, discussion rooms, undergraduate studios, a photography area, library and multi-purpose rooms — organised around campus pedestrian routes and plazas.

items.title: Dawn Light Church
items.titleZh: 曦光教堂 · 都市中的宗教建築
items.description: Concept “Light” — celebrating morning light and its daily changes. A central courtyard ties classrooms, an auditorium and the sanctuary together into a pure, bright home for anyone walking through darkness.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Aiguo W. Rd. & Guangzhou St., Taipei

sections.heading: Concept — Light
sections.text: The design celebrates morning light, sunlight and the everyday changes of light. When people are under pressure or walking through darkness, a church should be the first place they think of — a pure, bright place.

sections.heading: A Place of Warmth
sections.text: Whatever burdens you carry, coming to the church should bring a warm and happy moment, and anyone can come here to help those in need. A central courtyard ties together classrooms, an auditorium and the main sanctuary.

items.title: Mao'ao Ocean Culture Museum
items.titleZh: 卯不隆冬 · 海洋文化館
items.description: “Blending Nature and Culture: Heritage and Innovation.” Celebrating Mao'ao Bay's fishing culture through interactive exhibits and education, raising awareness of ocean protection and sustainable development.

sections.heading: Concept — Heritage and Innovation
sections.text: “Blending Nature and Culture.” The museum celebrates Mao'ao Bay's fishing culture through interactive exhibits and education.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: By bringing visitors to the water's edge, the project raises awareness of ocean protection and sustainable development while giving the fishing village a new place to share its story.

items.title: Anping Fishery & Fish Exhibition Hall
items.titleZh: 3D互動 — 安平漁與魚展覽館
items.description: Concept “Water” — the form is drawn from waves, spheres on the façade read as droplets that filter light, and reflecting pools make the building float. Inside: a 3D interactive fish zone and a water-curtain pool.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: East side of Anping Harbour, Tainan

facts.label: Theme
facts.value: 溯源地域 融合未來

sections.heading: Concept — Water
sections.text: Anping Harbour cannot be separated from water — its fishery and its fish live in and on the water — so the building's form is drawn from the shapes of waves.

sections.heading: Façade & Light
sections.text: The spheres on the façade represent crystal water droplets; light filters through the gaps between them into the interior. Reflecting pools around the base make the building appear to float on water.

sections.heading: Inside
sections.text: A 3D interactive fish zone, exhibitions, an indoor water-curtain pool and a seafood restaurant.

items.title: Huaxin Street Commercial District Renewal
items.titleZh: 商圈改造 · 中和華新街（南洋觀光美食街）
items.description: A multi-functional place that blends Southeast Asian culture with modern commerce — integrating food, retail and culture to lift the local economy and give residents and visitors a comfortable, attractive public space.

sections.heading: Vision
sections.text: A multi-functional place that blends Southeast Asian culture with modern commerce.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: Integrating food, retail and culture to lift the local economy and give residents and visitors a comfortable, attractive public space.

services.title: Architectural Design
services.text: Concept-driven design for hostels, schools, churches and museums — from site analysis to plans, sections and elevations.

services.title: BIM Modelling
services.text: Autodesk-certified Revit modelling, with hands-on BIM project experience from an internship at a BIM consultancy.

services.title: 3D Visualisation
services.text: Photoreal Lumion renderings of exteriors, interiors and landscapes that tell the story of a space.

services.title: Construction Management
services.text: Master's research in construction engineering & management at NTU, backed by site work as an engineering assistant.

about.lead: I design places where people meet and feel at home.
paragraphs: I'm Yang Qinyi (Quinn), born in northern Myanmar. In 2019 I came to Taiwan for the overseas Chinese preparatory program at NTNU, went on to study architecture at NTUST, and I'm now continuing with construction management research in Civil Engineering at National Taiwan University.

I'm optimistic and love sharing beautiful things with others. Drawing and calligraphy — especially sketching buildings and landscapes — taught me focus, and architectural design became my favourite subject, which led to my Autodesk certification.
